tellings.difference: This telling credits Paul Schatzkin's The Man Who Mastered Gravity rather than Aviation Week, gives no date, and frames the B-2 claim with Brown's deliberate disinformation: he showed people an ionic-wind fluid-dielectric system instead of the solid-dielectric gravitator.
tellings.link_reason: Both have Jesse Michels claiming that the B-2 stealth bomber uses Townsend Brown's electrogravitics (the Biefeld-Brown effect). The telling's 'we now even know' points to the same claim the story attributes to the 1992 Aviation Week report.

as_told.title: Electrohydrodynamics in the B-2 stealth bomber

plain: The B-2 stealth bomber, America's radar-dodging long-range bomber, is said to use the work of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown on using strong electric fields to push aircraft or move air around them, which Michels sometimes calls electric gravity. Michels tells this himself in several episodes, pointing to a story in the aviation trade magazine Aviation Week from March 1992, and also to Paul Schatzkin's biography of Brown, The Man Who Mastered Gravity, and to the researcher Paul LaViolette. In other tellings he adds that Brown spread false information to protect his work and that the defense company Northrop Grumman paid him off with a very small sum for the rest of his life.
